Saturday, September 19, 2026 · departing Jersey City

Two Roads Out of Jersey CityPick a river.

Two options — one is a foliage excursion, the second is a fall experience with fruit picking and views. The shortened version is constrained by the hours of operation for renting a car out of Newport. The full version is more flexible, given the 24-hour operation at the EWR rental location. Times are just estimates and are flexible to what we want to do and when we want to start.

Each option ends with a stop at a convenient Costco for gas, and a chance to use the $50 check.

Choose your day

1 h 10 min· 60 mi · I-78 W to US-202 S
1
Stop one · 3–4 hours

New Hope & the Railroad

New Hope Railroad, 32 W Bridge St, New Hope, PA 18938

Park once in the Bridge Street lots and do the whole town on foot — the walkable core is about six blocks. Two of the four things below are ticketed and run on fixed times; pick either one, then hang around the village.

Suggested stay · 3–4 h
  • Ride the excursion train. Cut in short version A 45-minute round trip through Bucks farmland in restored 1920s coaches, out of the 1891 station on Bridge Street.
    Traditional excursion · Sat Sep 19, 2026 First class $53  /  Coach $35
    11:00 AM12:00 PM1:00 PM2:00 PM3:00 PM
  • Pedal the rail bikes. Four-seat bikes on the tracks north of the station, through the woods and out along the creek. Ninety-minute windows, booked in advance — this is the one thing here that has to be reserved before you leave home.
    Rail bike experience · 90 min Adult 12+ from $67.50
    9:30 – 11:00 AM11:30 AM – 1:00 PM1:30 – 3:00 PM
    newhoperailroad.com/rail-bike-experience →
  • Walk the canal towpath at Bridge Street. Flat, shaded, and level with the water — go north as far as you like and turn around. Free, and the right thing to do in the gap between two booked slots.
  • Main Street browsing. Bookshops, record stores, and Gerenser's exotic ice cream. Bucks County Playhouse sits right on the river if a matinée fits.
10 min· 4 mi · US-202 N to Street Rd
2
Stop two · 1.5–2 hours Cut in short version

Peddler's Village

Peddler's Village, Lahaska, Pennsylvania 18938

A bunch of small shops with a lot of brick path and gardens.

Suggested stay · 1.5–2 h
  • Walk the garden loop. The whole village is a footpath — no traffic, benches everywhere, and planting that gets redone each season.
  • Giggleberry Fair carousel. A restored 1922 Philadelphia Toboggan Company carousel, indoors, running all year.
  • Late lunch. Buttonwood Grill for something proper, or the Cock 'n Bull for a lighter tavern plate.
  • If you're here in fall: the Scarecrow Festival runs mid-September through October.
25 min· 14 mi · PA-32 River Rd north
3
Stop three · 1 hour

Virginia Forrest Recreation Area

Virginia Forrest Recreation Area, Delaware Canal State Park, PA-32, Upper Black Eddy, PA

Walk along the Delaware river to enjoy the scenery.

Suggested stay · 1 h
  • Walk the towpath along the river. Dead flat crushed stone with water on both sides. Twenty minutes out and back is enough; the path continues for miles in either direction if you want more.
  • Sit at the river overlook. Picnic tables face the Delaware — bring something from Peddler's Village and eat here rather than in a restaurant.
1 h· 50 mi · PA-32 N to I-78 E

1 h 35 min· 85 mi · Palisades Pkwy to I-87 N, exit 18
1
Stop one · 1.5–2 hours

Jenkins-Lueken Orchards

69 Yankee Folly Rd, New Paltz, NY 12561 · U-pick Sat–Sun 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM

Pick first, eat after. The U-pick fields open at 9 and this is the least crowded you will find them all day.

Suggested stay · 1.5–2 h
  • 20+ apple varieties, with berries too. A wider varietal list than most orchards in the valley, and the picking rows are marked by variety.
  • 2026 U-pick season opened September 5. Running now through the fall, weather and crop permitting.
  • Main U-pick fields: Saturday and Sunday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM. Weekends only — worth confirming before a weekday attempt.
15 min· 7 mi · NY-299 E across town to N Ohioville Rd
2
Stop two · 2–3 hours

Twin Star Orchards

155 N Ohioville Rd, New Paltz, NY 12561

Eat lunch here. Book a table ahead on any weekend — walk-ins get turned away. Korean festival on September 19.

Suggested stay · 2–3 h
  • Wood-fired pizza on the lawn. Cooked in the outdoor oven, eaten at picnic tables looking out at the Shawangunk ridge.
  • Walk the orchard rows and say hello to the animals. Free to wander even outside picking season; live music most summer weekends.
  • Korea Festival · Sept 19, 12–6 PM · $30. twinstarorchards.com/korea-festival-2026 →
10 min· 4 mi · NY-299 W into the village
3
Stop three · 2 hours

New Paltz

New Paltz, New York 12561

Walk a local village and market. Potentially swing by Mohonk.

Suggested stay · 2 h
  • Wallkill Valley Rail Trail along the water. Pick it up where it crosses Main Street and head north across the trestle over the Wallkill — flat, shaded, and the best twenty minutes in town.
  • Mohonk Mountain House grounds to Sky Top. Cut in short version About 30 minutes up from the hotel grounds. Day visitors need a pass, so check availability before driving up.
  • Historic Huguenot Street. Seven original stone houses from the late 1600s on one block.
  • Sojourner Truth Park on the Wallkill. Riverside park at the foot of Main Street, where the rail trail meets the water.
  • Water Street Market. An antiques barn, a bookshop, and outdoor tables at the foot of the ridge.
  • Garvan's Gastropub for dinner if interested. Optional garvans.com/dinner →
14 min· 7 mi · NY-299 E to Haviland Rd, Highland
4
Stop four · optional · 1–1.5 hours Cut in short version

Walkway Over the Hudson

Walkway Over the Hudson State Historic Park, Highland entrance · 7:00 AM – 7:30 PM

Only if the day is running early — this is the first thing to cut.

Suggested stay · 1–1.5 h
  • Walk the full span and back. About 45 minutes at a normal pace. The deck is flat and fully accessible; there is no shade and it is windy, so bring a layer.
  • Enter from the Highland side. Closer coming from New Paltz, and the parking lot is bigger. Entry is free; parking runs a few dollars.
  • Open 7:00 AM – 7:30 PM. Last crossing needs to start by about 6:45 to get back across before closing.

Rental car

The pickup point sets the shape of the day. Newport is close by and costs nothing to reach, but nothing opens before 7:30. The airport opens earlier and has far more cars, at roughly $60 of round-trip rides.

🛠️ Simplest logistics

🚗 Newport rental

Close by · no ride needed

  • SIXT8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Avis7:30 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Budget7:30 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Estimated rate$109
  • No airport Uber or Lyft required — about $60 saved against the airport option.
  • The car itself costs more: $109 against roughly $47 at the airport, so the $60 of rides very nearly cancels out. Treat the two as the same price and choose on time.
  • Earliest possible departure is roughly 7:40 AM, and only with Avis or Budget.
  • Smaller fleet, so book early for a specific class of car.
Best for Route A / New Hope. The 7:30 pickup still lands you in New Hope before the 9:30 rail bike slot. On Route B the later start is the binding constraint — it is what forces the shortened plan.
⏱️ More flexible

✈️ Airport rental

Newark · ride each way

  • Opening~6:30 AM, some 24 h
  • Uber / Lyft each way~$30
  • Round trip~$60
  • Estimated rate€41 · ~$47
  • Much wider selection of cars than the Newport counters.
  • An hour earlier on the road, which is what makes the full itineraries fit.
  • Adds two rides to the day, at each end.
  • Cheaper car (€41, about $47) but roughly $60 of rides — about the same total as Newport once both are counted.
Best for Route B / New Paltz. The earlier start is what buys room for the second orchard, the village, and the Walkway Over the Hudson.

The two rentals cost about the same once you count the rides. Newport is $109 with no transport; the airport is about $47 plus roughly $60 of Uber, so around $107. A couple of dollars apart — pick on how early you want to leave, not on price.

Food and gas/tolls follow the route, not the rental choice: the two Route A rows share one figure and the two Route B rows share another, so those columns are not a reason to pick one rental over the other. The rental rate and the ride to the airport are.

Free either way: Peddler's Village, the Virginia Forrest towpath, New Paltz village and Historic Huguenot Street, the Wallkill Valley Rail Trail, and walking the Walkway itself. Mohonk requires a day pass, price not confirmed.

Drive times are estimates for a weekend morning departure and exclude traffic, tolls, and stops for gas.
Hours, ticketing, and reservation policies change seasonally — check ahead for the railroad, the orchard, and any restaurant.
